label: def:recovery-pressure
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:recovery-pressure}
We use \textbf{\emph{recovery pressure}} to denote the \emph{compression-induced functional structure underlying heterogeneity} in post-compression recovery responses.
head: environment
name: \redhead{Recovery pressure

label: def:finite_budget_recovery
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:finite_budget_recovery}
For compressed endpoint $c_0$ under intervention $\mathcal I$, let $D_t
=
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{val}}(c_t)
-
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{val}}(d_0)$ denote the remaining signed loss gap to the dense reference. We define
the \textbf{recovery response} at step $t$ as $H_t
=
D_0-D_t
=
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{val}}(c_0)
-
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{val}}(c_t),$ and characterize the finite-budget recoverability of $c_0$ under
$\mathcal I$ by the recovery-response trajectory $\mathcal H_T(c_0;\mathcal I)=\{H_t\}_{t=0}^{T}.$

label: prop:coordinate-preservation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:coordinate-preservation}
Any operator $\widetilde W_i$ produced by
Definition~\ref{def:fixed-coordinate} remains in the compression-selected
coordinate class $\widetilde W_i\in\mathcal F_i$. Consequently, $\operatorname{col}(\widetilde W_i)
\subseteq
\operatorname{col}(W_{2,i}),$ and $
\operatorname{row}(\widetilde W_i)
\subseteq
\operatorname{row}(W_{1,i}).$
    
                                    
           
                              
        
                                    
           
                              
    
If $C_i$ is nonsingular and $W_{2,i},W_{1,i}$ have full column and row rank,
respectively, both containments hold with equality.

name: Coordinate Preservation

label: def:backward-pressure
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:backward-pressure}
For recovery point $c_t$ and dense reference $d_0$, define the
compressed--dense loss-response contrast
\begin{equation}
p_t
=
\left.
\nabla_g
\Big[
\mathcal L_{\mathcal Q}(c_t[g])
-
\mathcal L_{\mathcal Q}(d_0[g])
\Big]
\right|_{g=\mathbf 1}.
\label{eq:pressure}
\end{equation}
We summarize this characterization by its overall magnitude
$P_t=\|p_t\|_2$ and its module-wise structure $q_{m,t}
=
\frac{\|p_{m,t}\|_2^2}{\|p_t\|_2^2},$ with $ p_t=\operatorname{concat}_{m\in\mathcal M}p_{m,t},$
$P_t>0.$ At the compression endpoint, these quantities are denoted $P_0$ and
$q_{m,0}$.
head: environment
name: Task-conditioned backward characterization

label: prop:local-sensitivity
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:local-sensitivity}
Let
$\Delta_t(g)=
\mathcal L_{\mathcal Q}(c_t[g])-
\mathcal L_{\mathcal Q}(d_0[g])$.
If $\Delta_t$ is differentiable at $g=\mathbf 1$, then for any perturbation
direction $v$,
\[
D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]=p_t^\top v,
\qquad
P_t
=
\max_{\|v\|_2\le 1}
\big|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\big|.
\]
Thus $P_t$ is the largest first-order compressed--dense difference in local
loss response under a unit Euclidean gate perturbation.
head: environment
name: Local sensitivity interpretation

label: prop:pressure-local
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pressure-local}
If $\Delta_t$ is differentiable at $g=\mathbf 1$, then for any perturbation
direction $v$,
\[
D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]=p_t^\top v,
\qquad
P_t
=
\max_{\|v\|_2\leq 1}
\left|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\right|.
\]
Thus $P_t$ is the largest first-order compressed--dense loss-response
difference under a unit Euclidean gate perturbation.
head: environment
name: Local sensitivity interpretation

title: Proof
body_md:
Because $\Delta_t$ is differentiable at $g=\mathbf 1$, its directional
derivative along any direction $v$ is given by $D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]
=
\left.
\nabla_g\Delta_t(g)
\right|_{g=\mathbf 1}^{\!\top} v
=
p_t^\top v,$ where the last equality follows from the definition
$p_t=\left.\nabla_g\Delta_t(g)\right|_{g=\mathbf 1}$. For any $v$ satisfying $\|v\|_2\leq 1$, Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
\left|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\right|
=
|p_t^\top v|
\leq
\|p_t\|_2\|v\|_2
\leq
\|p_t\|_2
=
P_t.
\]
Hence,
\[
\max_{\|v\|_2\leq 1}
\left|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\right|
\leq P_t.
\]

If $p_t\neq 0$, choosing
$v=p_t/\|p_t\|_2$ gives $\|v\|_2=1$ and
\[
\left|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\right|
=
\left|
p_t^\top\frac{p_t}{\|p_t\|_2}
\right|
=
\|p_t\|_2
=
P_t,
\]
so the upper bound is attained. If $p_t=0$, both sides are zero. Therefore, $P_t
=
\max_{\|v\|_2\leq 1}
\left|D\Delta_t(\mathbf 1)[v]\right|.$
